s_eg.title: Conformal Facies Interpretation from Well Logs with Stratigraphic-Grammar Decoding and Expert Referral
s_eg.abstract: Automatic facies interpretation from well logs is attractive for subsurface engineering, but a classifier that always returns a single label hides its uncertainty and can place facies in geologically impossible order. This paper presents StratGuard, a framework that returns a calibrated set of admissible facies at every depth and refers uncertain depths to a geologist. A base classifier is trained on gamma-ray, resistivity, density and neutron logs, and split conformal prediction converts its scores into prediction sets with a target coverage of 1−α. A Viterbi decoder, constrained to these sets and to an allowed stratigraphic transition grammar, then selects the facies sequence. Depths whose set size exceeds a threshold are flagged for expert review, and a cost-aware referral policy gives higher weight to errors near reservoir boundaries. Experiments on [dataset, N wells] with well-level splits report empirical coverage, referral rate and accuracy against the base classifier. The empirical coverage was [X] for a target of [1−α], the referral rate was [Y]%, and accuracy on non-referred depths rose from [A] to [B]. The decoder removed [Z]% of grammar-violating transitions. The results show that certified sets with constrained decoding can make machine-learning facies interpretation auditable, and that referral concentrates geologist effort where the model is uncertain.

s_ps.title: An Edge-to-Dashboard Framework for Anomaly Detection and Production Forecasting in Oil and Gas Fields
s_ps.abstract: Operators of mature oil and gas fields need to detect abnormal well and facility behaviour early, yet supervisory systems mostly raise fixed-threshold alarms that are either missed or ignored. This paper describes an intelligent field-monitoring framework that connects to SCADA through the OPC-UA and MQTT protocols and applies time-series analysis to wellhead pressure, temperature and production data. The framework combines unsupervised anomaly detection with short-horizon production forecasting and presents the results on a web dashboard that prioritises wells by deviation from expected behaviour. A demonstration deployment was set up on [number] wells of [field name] operated by [operator]. Over [period], the anomaly detector flagged [N] events, of which [M] were confirmed by field engineers, giving a precision of [X] and a recall of [Y] against the operator's alarm log. Production forecasts reached a mean absolute percentage error of [Z] at a [horizon] horizon, compared with [W] for [baseline]. The framework reduced the time needed to locate the cause of a deviation from [A] to [B] in the engineers' assessment. These findings show that a protocol-based, containerised monitoring layer can be added to existing field automation to support daily surveillance decisions, and they identify data quality at the wellhead as the main limit on accuracy.

s_pet.title: Machine-Learning Failure Prediction and Operating-Point Optimisation for Electric Submersible and Rod Lift Systems
s_pet.abstract: Artificial lift failures interrupt production and drive a large part of operating cost in mature oil fields. This paper presents an intelligent artificial-lift management system that predicts failures of electric submersible pumps (ESP) and rod pumps and recommends operating-point changes. Motor current, vibration, pressure and variable-speed-drive data are collected through Modbus and OPC-UA, converted into condition indicators, and used to train failure-prediction models for each lift type. A second module searches the feasible frequency and choke range for the operating point that maximises production under pump and reservoir constraints, and results are displayed on a web dashboard. The system was tested on historical data from [N] wells with [M] recorded failures. The failure model detected [X]% of failures with a median lead time of [Y] days and a false-alarm rate of [Z] per well-year, outperforming [baseline] on the same data. In simulated replays, the recommended operating points increased predicted production by [A]% without exceeding pump limits. The study shows that a single data pipeline can serve both condition monitoring and optimisation for different lift methods, and it discusses the labelling of failure events as the main practical difficulty.

s_iai.title: A Digital Twin with Soft Sensors for Grade-Transition Optimisation and Catalyst Degradation Prediction in a Petrochemical Plant
s_iai.abstract: Polyolefin plants switch between product grades several times a year, and each transition produces off-specification material while laboratory results for melt flow index (MFI) and density arrive hours late. This paper presents a digital twin for a petrochemical production line that combines soft sensors with transition-sequence optimisation and degradation forecasting. Soft sensors estimate MFI and density online from process measurements read from the distributed control system through OPC-UA. An optimiser then orders grade changes and proposes transition trajectories that shorten the off-specification period, and a separate model forecasts catalyst degradation and reactor fouling to support maintenance planning. The twin was developed with operating data from [plant, period] covering [N] grade transitions. The soft sensors achieved an error of [X] for MFI and [Y] for density against laboratory values. In replay of historical campaigns, the optimised sequence reduced estimated off-specification production by [Z]% relative to the actual sequence, and the degradation model gave [W] weeks of warning before the planned catalyst change. The results suggest that industrial AI built around a digital twin can turn delayed laboratory feedback into actionable guidance for operators, and the paper discusses requirements for deployment in closed-loop operation.

s_isie.title: Digital Twin and Data-Driven Condition Monitoring of Gas Turbine Compressors for Predictive Maintenance
s_isie.abstract: Gas turbines drive compressors and generators in oil, gas and power facilities, and unplanned outages are costly. This paper presents a digital twin that supports predictive maintenance of a gas turbine by combining a physics-based compressor performance model with data-driven anomaly detection and failure prediction. The performance model computes expected pressure ratio and efficiency from ambient and operating conditions, and the residual between model and measurement is used as a health indicator. Anomaly detection and failure-prediction algorithms process these residuals together with vibration and temperature signals, and a dashboard shows the health state and the predicted time to maintenance. The approach was evaluated on [dataset or plant] containing [N] operating hours and [M] labelled degradation events. The residual-based indicator detected compressor fouling [X] days earlier than a fixed-threshold alarm, with a false-alarm rate of [Y]. The failure predictor achieved an F1 score of [Z] compared with [W] for a purely data-driven baseline that does not use the performance model. The results show that coupling a performance model with learning methods improves early detection and keeps the indicators interpretable for maintenance engineers. The method is suitable for implementation on industrial edge hardware.

s_mimar.title: A Condition-Based Maintenance Dashboard with Traffic-Light Health Indices for Petrochemical and Refinery Assets
s_mimar.abstract: Maintenance teams in refineries and petrochemical plants must decide which of many assets need attention first, but raw condition data from vibration, temperature and process systems is difficult to interpret across equipment types. This paper describes a condition-based maintenance dashboard that converts such data into rule-based health indices shown as traffic-light states. Each asset class has a set of monitoring rules defined with maintenance engineers, and the indices are aggregated from component to unit level so that a planner can move from plant overview to the cause of an alert. The dashboard is built as a web application that connects to plant data sources through OPC-UA, MQTT and REST interfaces. We report the design of the rule base, the aggregation scheme and the interface, and an evaluation on [N] assets of [plant] over [period]. Alerts from the rules were compared with the maintenance work orders, and [X]% of work orders on the evaluated assets were preceded by a red or amber state with a median lead time of [Y] days, while [Z]% of alerts did not lead to action. Maintenance staff rated usefulness at [score] on a [scale]. The results indicate that transparent rule-based indices are an effective first stage before predictive models and give a basis for the reliability modelling of later stages.

s_icmhi.title: ReadmitCal: Calibration of Hospital Readmission Risk Models for Patients with Diabetes
s_icmhi.abstract: Hospital readmission risk models are used to allocate follow-up resources, but a model that ranks patients well can still give probabilities that are too high or too low, and this misleads clinical decisions. This paper studies the calibration of 30-day readmission risk models for patients with diabetes. We train logistic regression and gradient-boosting classifiers on routinely collected admission data from [UCI Diabetes 130-US hospitals, N encounters], using patient-level training, calibration and test splits so that no patient appears in two parts. Discrimination and calibration are compared before and after Platt scaling, isotonic regression and temperature scaling, and after the same methods fitted separately within subgroups defined by [insurance and age group]. Calibration is assessed with reliability curves, expected calibration error (ECE) and the Brier score, and clinical usefulness with decision-curve net benefit. The best classifier reached an AUC of [X], and its overall ECE was [Y]. The worst-subgroup ECE was [Z] before recalibration and fell to [W] with subgroup-wise recalibration, while AUC changed by [V]. Net benefit at thresholds of [range] was [B]. The results indicate that calibration should be reported and monitored for subgroups, and not only overall, when readmission models are used in health informatics systems; the open-source benchmark makes the comparison reproducible.

s_aimh.title: WearShift: Measuring and Reducing Distribution Shift in Wearable-Sensor Human Activity Recognition
s_aimh.abstract: Human activity recognition from wearable sensors is used in remote monitoring and rehabilitation, but models trained on one group of people or one device often lose accuracy on new users, sensor placements or sensors. This paper introduces WearShift, a benchmark and analysis framework for distribution shift in wearable activity recognition. We define cross-user (leave-one-user-out) and cross-device scenarios on [public datasets, e.g. UCI-HAR, WISDM, PAMAP2], extract window features from tri-axial accelerometer signals, and measure the change in macro-F1 relative to in-distribution testing together with a simple shift statistic between source and target features. We then compare three low-cost mitigation strategies against a baseline without adaptation: per-domain feature standardisation, correlation alignment (CORAL) and few-shot calibration with k labelled windows per activity. The in-distribution macro-F1 of [X] fell to [Y] under cross-user testing and to [Z] under cross-device testing. Standardisation recovered [W]% and CORAL [V]% of the lost performance without any labels, while few-shot calibration with k = [K] recovered [U]%. The findings show how much of the reported performance of wearable AI depends on the evaluation protocol, and they give a reproducible protocol for reporting robustness in medical and healthcare applications of such systems.

s_jimg.title: ExplainGuard: Testing the Faithfulness of Explanations for Medical Imaging Classifiers
s_jimg.abstract: Saliency maps and other post-hoc explanations are widely shown next to medical image predictions, yet they are rarely tested for whether they reflect what the model actually uses. This paper presents ExplainGuard, a framework that measures explanation faithfulness for medical imaging classifiers and flags explanations that should not be trusted. For a given classifier and explanation method, it applies deletion and insertion tests against random pixel orders, a weight-randomisation sanity check, and perturbation of the most and least relevant regions, and it summarises the results as a faithfulness score for each image. We evaluated gradient×input, occlusion and two negative controls (a random map and a model-independent edge map) on [dataset, task] with [model architecture]. Faithfulness scores varied by [X] between methods, and [Y]% of images received a score at or below that of random order. The edge map scored [Z] on deletion and insertion but failed the weight-randomisation check, so no single test was sufficient. Images with low scores had a [W] higher error rate. The results suggest that faithfulness testing should be routine in the validation of explainable AI for medical imaging; the open-source code applies the tests to any model with a probability output.

s_cmi.title: Attention-Based Fusion of Brain MRI and Biomarkers for Explainable Neurodegenerative Disease Risk Assessment
s_cmi.abstract: Early assessment of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease risk requires combining brain imaging with biomarkers and cognitive tests, but most imaging models use a single modality and give no explanation that a clinician can check. This paper presents an explainable multimodal framework that processes MRI with a convolutional neural network and processes biomarker and cognitive-test data with a multilayer perceptron. An attention-based fusion layer weights the two representations for each patient, and explanation maps and feature attributions are shown to the user together with the risk estimate. The framework is deployed as a web service connected to PACS and hospital information systems through DICOM and HL7/FHIR. We evaluated it on [dataset, N subjects] using subject-level cross-validation. The fused model reached an AUC of [X] for [disease/task], compared with [Y] for the MRI-only model and [Z] for the biomarker-only model. Attention weights showed that [pattern], and explanation maps highlighted [regions] in agreement with [clinical reference]. [N] clinicians rated the explanations as useful in [X]% of cases. These results show that attention-based fusion can improve risk assessment over single-modality models while keeping decisions inspectable.

s_npj.title: A Digital Pharmacogenomics Platform that Converts Sequencing Data into Electronic Health Record-Ready Drug Guidance
s_npj.abstract: Pharmacogenomic results rarely reach prescribers in a form they can act on. We developed a platform that processes sequencing reads (FASTQ/BAM) through quality control, alignment, variant calling and annotation, applies machine-learning interpretation, and returns structured JSON guidance for electronic health records. Privacy-preserving synthetic genomic data generated with a Gaussian copula supports development and testing without patient data. We evaluated variant-calling concordance on [reference set], interpretation accuracy against [guideline, e.g., CPIC] for [N] gene–drug pairs, and turnaround time on [N] samples. Concordance with the reference was [X]%, interpretation agreed with the guideline in [Y]% of cases, and median turnaround was [Z] hours. Pharmacists judged the reports actionable in [W]% of cases. The platform shows that a containerised pipeline can deliver guideline-concordant pharmacogenomic guidance within the clinical workflow, and prospective studies of prescribing outcomes are needed.

s_qip.title: StretchWatch: How Good Is the Hartree–Fock Starting Point for VQE Along Bond-Stretching Curves?
s_qip.abstract: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) is usually started from the Hartree–Fock (HF) state, but HF becomes a poor approximation of the ground state when bonds are stretched and electron correlation grows. We quantify this effect for small molecules, H2, HeH+ and LiH, in the STO-3G basis with the Jordan–Wigner mapping. For each bond length we compute the exact ground state by full configuration interaction, the overlap between the HF state and the ground state, and the entanglement entropy of the natural orbitals, and we combine overlap and entropy into a starting-point quality index. From these curves we determine the bond length beyond which HF is no longer a suitable starting state and we test an automatic switch to an alternative reference state such as CISD. The overlap fell below [X] at a bond length of [Y] Å for [molecule], and the quality index predicted the number of VQE iterations needed to reach chemical accuracy with a correlation of [Z]. The poster will show the curves, the threshold and the switching rule, and the code is released for reproduction. The study is a methodological benchmark on simulators and makes no claim of quantum advantage.

s_front_nuc.title: A Physics-Informed Digital Twin for Predictive Maintenance and Transient Forecasting of Nuclear Reactors
s_front_nuc.abstract: Nuclear reactors require continuous monitoring and conservative maintenance decisions, and purely data-driven models are difficult to accept in a safety-regulated setting because they ignore the underlying physics and give no uncertainty estimate. This work proposes a digital twin of a nuclear reactor that combines physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), an extended Kalman filter (EKF) and a hybrid LSTM–ARIMA model. The PINN encodes the governing reactor-kinetics and thermal-hydraulic relations as constraints in training, so that state estimates remain physically consistent when measurements are scarce. The EKF fuses the PINN prediction with sensor measurements to estimate hidden states and their uncertainty in real time. The LSTM–ARIMA model forecasts the evolution of operating transients, with the ARIMA part capturing linear trend and the LSTM part capturing the nonlinear residual. A decision-support layer converts the state estimates and forecasts into maintenance recommendations with confidence bounds that remain under operator control. The twin was tested on [simulated/experimental data from facility or code] covering [scenarios, e.g., power ramp, load-following, sensor fault]. Against a purely data-driven LSTM, the physics-informed twin reduced the transient forecasting error from [X] to [Y] and kept state-estimate violations of the physical constraints below [Z]. Under injected sensor faults, the filter detected the fault after [W] seconds. The results show that combining physics-based constraints with filtering and forecasting improves accuracy and reliability, and they outline the verification and validation needed before use in an operating plant, where the system is intended to support and not replace licensed operators.

s_mie.title: A Scalable Incremental ETL and Machine-Learning Platform for Health Big Data Using HL7/FHIR and DICOM
s_mie.abstract: Hospitals and health networks hold clinical, imaging and laboratory data in separate systems and formats, which limits the use of machine learning for clinical decision support. This paper presents a big-data analytics platform for health that ingests data in HL7/FHIR, DICOM and CSV formats and loads it through an incremental extract-transform-load pipeline. The platform uses Kafka for streaming ingestion, Spark for distributed processing, object storage for imaging files and scheduled workers for recurring jobs, and exposes clinical machine-learning models and cohort analytics through an interactive dashboard. Patient identifiers are pseudonymised on ingestion and access is role-based. We evaluated the platform on [dataset, N records] by measuring ingestion throughput, incremental-load time and model performance for [clinical prediction task]. The pipeline processed [X] records per second and reduced the daily refresh time from [Y] to [Z] compared with full reloads. The prediction model reached an AUC of [W] on a held-out set. The results show that a standards-based incremental architecture can make heterogeneous health data available for analytics at reasonable cost, and they point to data harmonisation as the main effort in deployment.

s_jpse.title: Intelligent Inventory Monitoring and Leak Detection for Storage Tanks and Pipeline Terminals
s_jpse.abstract: Storage terminals and the pipelines that feed them lose product through slow leaks and measurement errors that are hard to separate from normal inventory movement. This paper presents an intelligent monitoring system for terminals and tanks that reconciles measured tank levels, temperatures and transfer flows to maintain a continuous inventory balance, and that detects leaks from the persistent residual of this balance. The system collects data from level gauges and flow meters, corrects volumes for temperature, and applies statistical change detection to the residual to separate leaks from gauge noise and from transfers. Alarms are ranked by estimated loss rate and are shown on a monitoring dashboard together with the supporting balance. The method was evaluated on [data source] covering [N] tanks over [period], including [M] real or injected leaks of [size range]. The system detected leaks of [X] L/h or more with a detection delay of [Y] hours and a false-alarm rate of [Z] per tank-year, compared with [W] for a fixed-threshold balance check. The results indicate that residual-based inventory reconciliation gives earlier and more reliable leak warnings than threshold checks, and the paper discusses sensor calibration and the minimum detectable leak rate as the main limits for pipeline and terminal operators.

s_iqim.title: HQCA: A Software Platform for Hybrid Quantum–Classical Drug Discovery on Quantum Simulators
s_iqim.abstract: Researchers who want to test quantum algorithms for drug discovery need a workflow that links molecular data, classical pre-processing, quantum circuits and result analysis in one reproducible environment. This paper presents HQCA, a software platform for hybrid quantum–classical drug discovery. A web service built with FastAPI manages jobs, data and results; a processing layer prepares ligand and protein descriptors, encodes them with angle embedding into variational quantum circuits, and trains them with the COBYLA optimiser; and a VQE module estimates ground-state energies of small fragments. The quantum layer is executed on Qiskit Aer and PennyLane simulators, and the platform is deployed with Docker Compose together with object storage and a web dashboard that displays molecules in three dimensions. We describe the architecture, the data flow and the interfaces to future quantum hardware back ends. As an evaluation, we ran [N] binding-prediction experiments on [dataset] and report runtime, scaling with qubit count up to [Q] qubits, and accuracy relative to classical baselines of [type]. Runtime grew by [X] for each added qubit and the best variational model reached [metric] of [Y]. The results show the feasibility of the workflow and the limits of simulation, and the platform provides a basis for studies on real devices.

s_iqicsa.title: Shot-Budget Lab: Comparing Uniform, Weighted and Classical-Shadow Measurement Allocation for Pauli-Sum Observables
s_iqicsa.abstract: Estimating the expectation value of a Hamiltonian on a quantum computer requires many repeated measurements, and the way a fixed shot budget is divided among the Pauli terms determines the accuracy of the estimate. This paper presents Shot-Budget Lab, a reproducible simulation framework that compares three allocation strategies for Pauli-sum observables: uniform allocation, weighted allocation proportional to the coefficient magnitude or to the term variance, and classical shadows based on random Pauli measurements. For systems of three to eight qubits we generate random Hamiltonians and states, run each strategy at equal total shot budget, and report root-mean-square error and bias against the exact value. We also evaluate an adaptive strategy that estimates the posterior variance of each term after a pilot round and divides the remaining budget accordingly. Across [N] Hamiltonians the weighted strategy reduced the RMSE by [X]% relative to uniform allocation at a budget of [S] shots, classical shadows were [better/worse] when [condition], and the adaptive strategy gave a further [Y]% reduction. The results give practical guidance on choosing a measurement strategy for near-term quantum simulation and applications, and the framework is released with its configuration files for reproduction.

s_quantics.title: QRNG-Audit: Device-Level Statistical Auditing of Quantum Random Number Generators with False-Discovery-Rate Control
s_quantics.abstract: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are used in communication and security systems, and their output must be checked continuously because a faulty device can produce biased or correlated bits. Applying a battery of statistical tests to many bit strings and flagging any string with a small p-value causes many false alarms at the device level. This paper presents QRNG-Audit, an auditing framework that runs five basic statistical tests on each bit string (frequency, runs, longest run, poker and autocorrelation), collects the p-values for each device and circuit, and applies Benjamini–Hochberg correction to control the false discovery rate. The framework returns a healthy or unhealthy verdict per device and reports a calibrated health score, including the empirical false-alarm rate measured on ideal sources. We evaluated the method on [N] bit strings of length [L] from [public QRNG data and synthetic sources], including ideal, biased and correlated generators. The false-alarm rate on ideal sources was [X] at a target FDR of [q], and the detection rate was [Y] for a bias of [b] and [Z] for a correlation of [c]. The results show that device-level correction gives reliable verdicts at low cost, and the implementation processes 1000 strings of 1024 bits in under [T] seconds without heavy dependencies.

s_icqe.title: QGrid-Part: QAOA versus Classical Methods for Partitioning Power Networks into Two Islands
s_icqe.abstract: Splitting a power network into two islands is a way to limit the spread of a disturbance, and it can be written as a weighted MaxCut problem on the network graph. This paper investigates whether the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA) offers a useful alternative to classical partitioning heuristics for this task. We build a framework that loads a network as a weighted graph, forms the MaxCut Hamiltonian, runs QAOA with depth p from 1 to 3 using exact state-vector simulation, and compares it with greedy and spectral bisection. Quality is reported as the approximation ratio with respect to the best known cut, together with the quantum resources used: qubits and circuit depth. A structured post-processing step based on graph repair restores generation–load balance in each island. Experiments were run on the IEEE 14-bus topology and on [N] synthetic networks of up to 14 buses. QAOA at p = [p] reached an approximation ratio of [X], compared with [Y] for greedy and [Z] for spectral bisection, and the repair step reduced the imbalance from [A] to [B] MW. We discuss what these small-scale simulations do and do not imply for quantum computing in energy systems, and the framework is provided as a transparent benchmark.

s_hydro.title: HydroGate: Does Hydrograph-State Gating Improve Seven-Day Streamflow Forecasts?
s_hydro.abstract: Streamflow behaves differently on the rising limb, during recession and in stable periods, and it is often proposed to use a separate forecasting model for each hydrograph state. This study tests that idea as a reproducible benchmark. For five public USGS rivers (or equivalent synthetic series), we build seven-day-ahead forecasts from lagged flows and seasonal sine–cosine features. A global gradient-boosting model is compared with a hard-gated model, in which the hydrograph state of the current day (rising, receding or stable, from a three-day moving-average slope) selects a state-specific model, and with persistence as a baseline. Performance is measured by RMSE and Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE). The global model reached a median NSE of [X] across stations, compared with [Y] for persistence and [Z] for the gated model. The gated model [improved/did not improve] on the global model at [N] of five stations, and the difference was [due to … /small compared with the uncertainty from random seeds]. A soft, fuzzy-weighted combination of the state-specific models is also examined. We report negative results openly, because they show when gating is not worth its added complexity, and all code and data-generation scripts are provided for reproduction.
